label: copy-phase input c or i (from the 3rd copied token on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original phase or on <DEL>), when the fed-back input token is c or i (together about 95% of activation mass). The firing rate is near zero for the first copied tokens (recall_idx 0-1) and levels off around 5.5% for recall_idx >= 3, so later positions fire more. The strongest examples are mostly an input c whose output at that step is i (i.e. a c i bigram in the original), followed by the i itself. out_tok == i has a 7.3x lift. A few weak activations land on the step just before an i is fed back (input x/j/f while outputting i). Does not fire on c/i in the original phase or on other tokens. Precision is only about 0.69: many copy-phase c/i inputs stay silent, and no simple variable I tried (to_go, in_count, splitting c vs i) separates them. Dev F1 0.78, mass recall 0.95.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=11: c, i, x, j; t=9: c, i, x, j; t=10: c, i, x, j) and the token being output (most: i, j, c, r, x, d; least: b, e, k, q); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4.
